{< include ../exercise-header.qmd >}


::: {#exr-walrus-sail-linen}
DISCUSSION: Imagine two gamblers. One has been at the table for a long time without winning. The other has just arrived. Are the gamblers justified in having different expectations about how likely is a win in the near future? Suppose the newly-arrived gambler doesn't know how long the other gambler has been playing.  Does that make a difference? Wouldn't this suggest that after a win, the gambler should leave the table and move to another where a win hasn't happened in a while?
:::
 <!-- end of exr-walrus-sail-linen -->
